title_en: Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Art Printing Co., Ltd. v. Guanjiao Central Printing Factory — dispute over patent infringement

full_text_en:
Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Fine Arts Printing Co., Ltd. v. Guanjiao Central Printing Factory — dispute over patent infringement

Plaintiff: Zhuang Zhihe, male, 37 years old, a resident of Beijing.

Agent ad litem: Hua Changrong, Deputy General Manager of Shenzhen Tianming Fine Arts Printing Co., Ltd., Guangdong Province.

Plaintiff: Shenzhen Tianming Fine Arts Printing Co., Ltd., Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xie Shaojing, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Guo Weigang, Patent Agent of Shenzhen Patent Service Center, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Sai Ji, Attorney at Law of Zhenchang Law Firm, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: Guanjiao Central Printing Factory, Nanhai City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Jijun, Factory Director of the factory.

Agent ad litem: Cao Weilong, Attorney at Law of Nanyue Law Firm, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: He Haifan, Senior Engineer of Guangdong Patent Agency.

Plaintiffs Zhuang Zhihe and Shenzhen Tianming Fine Arts Printing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianming Company) filed a lawsuit with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province, against Defendant Guanjiao Central Printing Factory, Nanhai City, Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as Guanjiao Printing Factory) for patent infringement.

Plaintiffs Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company alleged: "Rice paper printed products and offset plate-making and printing method therefor" is a patent right obtained by Plaintiff Zhuang Zhihe on December 30, 1995. Zhuang Zhihe granted Plaintiff Tianming Company a three-year nationwide exclusive exploitation license and a non-exclusive exploitation license thereafter. Both plaintiffs have the right to pursue infringement actions against any third party. Without permission, Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory produced and sold simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper for two consecutive years, which infringed both Zhuang Zhihe's patent right and Tianming Company's exclusive right to use. Therefore, the plaintiffs prayed for judgment: 1. That Guanjiao Printing Factory immediately cease the infringement and stop printing and selling the infringing products; 2. That Guanjiao Printing Factory compensate the two plaintiffs for economic losses of RMB 200,000; 3. That Guanjiao Printing Factory publicly apologize to the two plaintiffs; 4. That the litigation costs be borne by Guanjiao Printing Factory.

Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory argued: 1. The plaintiffs' patent contains content and items that constitute grounds for invalidation under Article 66 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, and has lost novelty and inventiveness, and thus should not have been granted a patent right. 2. The plaintiffs incorporated prior art into the scope of patent protection, violating the provisions of the Patent Law and harming the public interest. 3. The printing plate used by our factory was manufactured using the ICR-30 process, which is more advanced than the plaintiffs' patent. Since the plate manufacturer has not been sued for infringement, there is no reason to hold our factory liable for infringement. The paper used by our factory is simulated rice paper, not the rice paper defined by the plaintiffs. The main technical parameters of our factory differ from the plaintiffs' patent in six major aspects, and there is no issue of sales or method infringement. In summary, our factory has not infringed the plaintiffs' patent, and we request the court to render a fair decision.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court found the following facts through trial:

On November 15, 1993, Plaintiff Zhuang Zhihe filed an invention patent application with the Chinese Patent Office for "Rice paper printed products and offset plate-making and printing method therefor." On December 30, 1995, the Chinese Patent Office granted Zhuang Zhihe Patent No. ZL93114279.2 and published the patent on January 10, 1996. The claims of the patent are:

1. A rice paper printed product, on which patterns of works such as traditional Chinese painting, calligraphy, and seal carving are printed, characterized in that the patterns are printed on the said rice paper using offset printing ink by means of modern offset printing equipment including an electronic color scanner, an offset printing press, and a proofing machine, through steps such as color separation, image assembly, plate copying, proofing, and printing.

2. A method of offset plate-making and printing for printing the rice paper printed product according to claim 1, comprising the steps of color separation, image assembly, plate copying, proofing, and printing, said method being characterized in that:
in said color separation step, a screen of 200-250 lines per square inch is used for plate-making, and when performing color separation with an electronic color scanner, the unsharp masking (USM) key is adjusted to 0-4 or 0-5, and the background color of the original is removed;
before carrying out said proofing and printing steps, the rice paper used for proofing or printing is laid flat for about one day in an environment with a temperature of 25°C ± 2°C and a humidity of 70% ± 10%;
in said proofing step, original box ink is used, and the distance between the impression cylinder and the paper table is set to 7-8U, and a sheet of coated paper is placed under the said rice paper during proofing;
before said printing step, thin rice paper is first mounted on thick paper such as coated paper or offset paper, i.e., the front and back edges are pasted together for printing, and thick rice paper can be printed directly;
in said printing step, the suction air volume is adjusted to 7-8 kg, and the printing speed is set to 2000-4000 impressions per hour.

On December 15, 1993, Plaintiff Zhuang Zhihe entered into a contract with Plaintiff Tianming Company to license the technology of his patent application to Tianming Company for use. The contract stipulated: The transfer and license of the patent application technology included a nationwide exclusive license for three years and a non-exclusive exploitation license thereafter. The transfer and license fee consisted of an initial payment of RMB 300,000 and sales royalties. After the patent application technology was granted a patent right, both parties had the right to prevent any third party from infringement and could jointly seek economic compensation from the infringing party through litigation or other legal means. The economic compensation obtained was to be shared equally between the two parties.

On December 1, 1996, Plaintiff Zhuang Zhihe entered into another contract with Plaintiff Tianming Company to license the patented technology of "Rice paper printed products and offset plate-making and printing method therefor" to Tianming Company for use. The contract stipulated: The transfer and license of the patented technology included a nationwide exclusive license for one year and a non-exclusive exploitation license thereafter. The exploitation license fee was to be paid in the form of sales royalties at a rate of 5% of sales revenue. If it was found that a third party had infringed this patent, both parties should promptly notify each other and jointly stop the infringement and claim economic compensation through litigation or other legal means. The economic compensation obtained was to be shared equally between the two parties.

There was no dispute between Plaintiff Zhuang Zhihe and Plaintiff Tianming Company regarding the performance of the above-mentioned contracts for the exploitation license of the patent application technology and the patented technology.

Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory began producing and selling simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper in 1995. By the end of May 1997, it had produced and sold approximately 100,000 copies of such calendars and was still producing them upon customer requests. The court commissioned the Shenzhen Intellectual Property Research Association to organize an expert panel to appraise the simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper produced by Guanjiao Printing Factory. The conclusion was: The technical features involved in the rice paper calendars produced by Guanjiao Printing Factory and the method of producing them fell within the scope of patent protection of invention patent No. 93114279, "Rice paper printed products and offset plate-making method therefor." An audit of the cost and profit of Guanjiao Printing Factory's production and sale of simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper showed that from January 1996 to May 1997, the profit from such production and sale was RMB 100,988.40. During the trial, Plaintiffs Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company expressly stated that they waived their claims for the profits earned by Guanjiao Printing Factory from the production and sale of simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper after May 1997 and would not pursue them in this case.

The above facts are confirmed by the patent certificate, the contract for the exploitation license of the patent application technology, the contract for the exploitation license of the patented technology, the technical consultation opinion, the audit report, and the trial transcripts.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court held:

The invention patent right for "Rice paper printed products and offset plate-making and printing method therefor" obtained by Plaintiff Zhuang Zhihe on December 30, 1995, is entitled to legal protection. By entering into a contract, Zhuang Zhihe and Plaintiff Tianming Company agreed that Tianming Company had the right to jointly sue the infringing party together with Zhuang Zhihe. This agreement does not violate the law, so Tianming Company is a proper plaintiff in this case together with Zhuang Zhihe.

Article 11 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "After the grant of a patent right for an invention or utility model, except as otherwise provided for by law, no entity or individual may, without the authorization of the patentee, make, use, or sell the patented product, or use the patented method and use or sell the product directly obtained by the patented method for production or business purposes." Article 59 provides: "The scope of protection of the patent right for an invention or utility model shall be determined by the terms of the claims. The description and the appended drawings may be used to interpret the claims." Without the permission of the patentee, Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory produced and sold simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper. According to expert appraisal, these calendars fell within the scope of protection of Plaintiff Zhuang Zhihe's Patent No. ZL93114279.2. Therefore, the actions of Guanjiao Printing Factory constitute infringement. Article 118 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If the copyright (copyright), patent right, trademark exclusive right, right of discovery, right of invention, or other scientific and technological achievements right of a citizen or legal person is infringed upon by such acts as plagiarism, alteration, or counterfeiting, the victim has the right to request the cessation of the infringement, the elimination of its effects, and compensation for losses." Guanjiao Printing Factory shall bear the corresponding civil liability for the consequences of its infringement. Given that Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company have expressly stated that they will not pursue the profits earned by Guanjiao Printing Factory from the production and sale of simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper after May 1997, the infringement compensation amount is limited to the profits earned by Guanjiao Printing Factory from January 1996 to the end of May 1997. The request of the two plaintiffs for compensation of RMB 200,000 from Guanjiao Printing Factory is insufficiently supported and is not granted. The other requests are reasonable and are supported.

In summary, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 5, 1998:

1. Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory shall immediately cease the production and sale of simulated traditional Chinese painting calendars on rice paper.

2. Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory shall compensate Plaintiffs Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 100,988.40.

3. Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory shall publicly apologize to Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company in the "Southern Daily."

4. The other claims of Plaintiffs Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company are dismissed.

The litigation costs of RMB 30,510 are to be borne by Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Defendant Guanjiao Printing Factory refused to accept it and appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court. The reasons for the appeal were: 1. The appellant used painting and calligraphy paper, not the rice paper within the scope of the appellee's patent protection, in producing the calendars. The appellant's printing method, such as the ink used in plate-making and printing, the temperature and humidity of the paper, and the printing speed, all differ from the appellee's patent. Therefore, the appellant does not infringe the appellee's patent right. 2. Looking at the appellee's patent itself, except for "rice paper," the rest are traditional publicly available technologies that lack novelty and inventiveness. The appellee's appropriation of publicly known technology hinders the public interest and should not be protected by law. This patent is currently under review by the Chinese Patent Office and should be revoked. 3. The subject matter of this case is RMB 200,000, but the first-instance court collected litigation costs of RMB 30,510, which has no legal basis and should be corrected. The appellant's requests on appeal were: 1. To set aside the original judgment and render a new judgment according to law; 2. To entrust a specialized agency to re-appraise the disputed patent, suspend the proceedings, and wait for the Chinese Patent Office's decision before proceeding; 3. To verify the litigation costs in this case and order the appellees to bear them.

The appellees argued in their defense that the appellant's infringement was established, the original judgment was correct, and it should be affirmed.

The Guangdong High People's Court found the following in its second-instance trial:

When the first-instance court commissioned the Shenzhen Intellectual Property Research Association to organize experts to appraise the technical issues related to the calendars produced by both parties, the experts visited the site and learned the offset plate-making method of the appellant Guanjiao Printing Factory as follows: (1) Using blended ink for color correction printing. (2) Printing speed of 4500 impressions per hour. (3) Suction air volume less than 7 kg. (4) Direct machine printing. (5) Screen ruling of 200 lines per inch. (6) Unsharp masking value between 6-8 or 10-18. The expert consultation opinion once stated: Guanjiao Printing Factory used the invention patent of Zhuang Zhihe, which defines rice paper printed products utilizing commonly used modern offset printing equipment and technology, i.e., using an electronic color scanner, offset printing press, and proofing machine, through the steps of electronic color separation, image assembly, plate copying, proofing, and printing, to produce simulated painting and calligraphy printed products on non-printing rice paper or modified rice paper, which falls within the scope of claim 1, a product independent claim defined by method features. Regarding claim 2, the experts also considered that the technical features of the two parties had differences but no substantive differences. Therefore, the appraisal conclusion was: The technical features of the rice paper calendars produced by Guanjiao Printing Factory and the method of producing them fell within the scope of patent protection of invention patent No. 93114279, "Rice paper printed products and offset plate-making method therefor."

During the first-instance proceedings, the appellee Tianming Company paid appraisal fees and audit fees of RMB 10,000 and RMB 15,000 to the Shenzhen Intellectual Property Research Association and Shenzhen Yongming Accounting Firm, respectively.

On August 20, 1998, the Chinese Patent Office issued a "Notice of Examination Opinion on a Request for Revocation of the Patent Right," stating that claim 1 of the disputed patent lacked inventiveness. If the patentee agreed to delete claim 1, the patent would be maintained on the basis of claim 2; if the patentee disagreed to delete it, the patent might be revoked in its entirety. On May 7, 1999, the Chinese Patent Office issued a "Decision on Examination of a Request for Revocation of the Patent Right," deciding to revoke the original claim 1 of Patent No. ZL93114279.2 and maintain the original claim 2. Because original claim 1 was revoked, the description in original claim 2, "A method of offset plate-making and printing for printing the rice paper printed product according to claim 1," had to be revised to "A method of offset plate-making and printing for printing patterns of works such as traditional Chinese painting, calligraphy, and seal carving on rice paper," with the following text remaining the same as the original claim 2.

Apart from this, the second-instance trial confirmed all the facts found in the first-instance trial.

The Guangdong High People's Court held:

The ZL93114279.2 "Rice paper printed products and offset plate-making and printing method therefor" patent granted to the appellee Zhuang Zhihe by the Chinese Patent Office on December 30, 1995, contained two items: one was a product independent claim, and the other was a method independent claim. On May 7, 1999, the Chinese Patent Office issued a "Decision on Examination of a Request for Revocation of the Patent Right," which changed the claims of the patent. Therefore, the scope of protection of the patent should no longer be based on the scope of protection at the time of grant on December 30, 1995, but on the final text determined by the Chinese Patent Office on May 7, 1999. Thus, to determine whether the appellant Guanjiao Printing Factory infringed the patent right of the appellee Zhuang Zhihe, it should be considered whether the method used by the appellant fell within the scope of protection of Zhuang Zhihe's method patent.

The appellant Guanjiao Printing Factory's argument that the appellee Zhuang Zhihe's patent was publicly known technology not protected by law lacks factual basis and is not adopted.

Upon comparing the offset plate-making method of the appellant Guanjiao Printing Factory with the patented method of the appellee Zhuang Zhihe, it is confirmed that there are obvious differences between them. Specifically: Guanjiao Printing Factory printed directly on the machine without specifying temperature and humidity, whereas the patent requires the rice paper to be laid flat for about one day in an environment with a temperature of 25°C ± 2°C and a humidity of 70% ± 10% before printing, and thin rice paper is first mounted on thick paper such as coated paper or offset paper. In the color separation step, Guanjiao Printing Factory used a screen ruling of 200 lines per inch and an unsharp masking value between 6-8 or 10-18, whereas the patent uses a screen ruling of 200-250 lines per square inch and adjusts the USM key to 0-4 or 0-5. In the printing step, Guanjiao Printing Factory adjusted the suction air volume to less than 7 kg and the printing speed to 4500 impressions per hour, whereas the patent adjusts the suction air volume to 7-8 kg and the printing speed to 2000-4000 impressions per hour. It is evident that the offset plate-making method used by Guanjiao Printing Factory did not completely cover all the essential technical features described in the claims of the amended Patent No. ZL93114279.2. The appraisal conducted by experts commissioned by the first-instance court was made under the premise that the original claim 1 of the disputed Patent No. ZL93114279.2 still existed before the patent was amended. Under the new circumstances after the patent was amended, this conclusion has lost the necessary reference basis for the appraisal and is therefore not adopted. The appellant Guanjiao Printing Factory's appeal argument that its method of producing rice paper calendars did not fall within the scope of protection of the disputed patent is well-founded and is adopted. The claims of Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company that Guanjiao Printing Factory's actions infringed their patent right lack factual and legal basis and are not supported.

The appellant Guanjiao Printing Factory argued that the subject matter of this case was only RMB 200,000, and the first-instance court should not have collected litigation costs of RMB 30,510. Upon verification, the first-instance court strictly followed the rules and pre-collected a case acceptance fee of RMB 5,510, and the remaining RMB 25,000 was for audit fees and appraisal fees. Therefore, the first-instance court did not over-collect litigation costs. The appellant's appeal request regarding the collection of litigation costs is inconsistent with the facts and is not credible.

In summary, the facts found in the original judgment are clear, but given that during the second-instance trial, the Chinese Patent Office revoked part of the claims of the disputed patent, the scope of patent protection on which the original judgment was based has changed. It is necessary to determine whether there is infringement based on the new patent claims. Therefore, this case is subject to a modified judgment. Accordingly, the Guangdong High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on June 30, 1999:

1. The first-instance civil judgment is set aside.

2. The claims of Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company are dismissed.

The first-instance and second-instance case acceptance fees total RMB 11,020, appraisal fees of RMB 10,000, and audit fees of RMB 15,000, totaling RMB 36,020, are to be borne by Zhuang Zhihe and Tianming Company.
